applied.problem: It calls the traced sine wave the shape of an AC supply's voltage outright; a real supply only closely follows a sine (the lesson's own ignores says so), and this sentence is read alone in the dossier.
Worked example: 325.3 × sin 0.785 on a calculator gives 229.9 V, not 230.0 (0.785 is rounded π/4); also the supply is ideal, not exact, and the find-the-time steps miss a + φ and later waves.
